_why: EVERY PERSON'S URL, FROZEN. Written once per person and never recomputed.
build-people.py derived the slug on every run with `seen[base] += 1` and
`base-{seen[base]}`, counted in the ROW ORDER OF data/lerena-register.tsv.
Insert a row above a namesake and every namesake below it is renumbered.
This archive has not been bitten yet only because nobody has reordered
that file; the Blazevic archive minted the same way and six men swapped
URLs with each other between two commits in September.
THE KEY IS THE NAME, AND THAT IS A COMPROMISE WORTH STATING. All 357 name
strings here are distinct — this register already does its person-
identification inside the name, «Alejandro LERENA (m. Elisa
VILLARDEMOROS)», «Bernabe LERENA (the elder, of the 1911 diagram)» — so
the name is a working identity today. It is not a good one. Correct a
name and the key moves with it, which is the fault this file exists to
prevent, merely made rarer: it now takes an edit to THAT person rather
than an edit to anybody above them.
THE REAL FIX IS A MINTED ID IN data/lerena-register.tsv — a column written
once per row and never reused — after which this ledger should be rekeyed
onto it and the name demoted to a label. That is a change to this
archive's central file and belongs to whoever owns it.
A slug is never edited and never deleted, because a published URL is a
promise and the address must not pass to a different person.
Seeded 23 September 2026 from the slugs the site was already serving.
The position is the Defranceski archive's, of the same day: a page is a
person, an id is frozen, a name is an index.
11 OCTOBER 2026 - THE FIRST RENAME AND THE FIRST MERGE, AND WHAT WAS DONE.
A surname this archive had read as ZALSAMENDI turned out to be ZALDUONDO on both
plates, and 'Amelia LERENA' turned out to be ANGELICA MARIA LERENA VILLADEMOROS.
That is exactly the fault named above: correct a name and the key moves with it.
FIVE PUBLISHED SLUGS WERE ORPHANED. They are KEPT here, never deleted, and their
addresses are kept alive by redirects in site/astro.config.mjs - the same device
this estate already used on 9 October for two folded pages. A reader who followed
/people/eduardo-zalsamendi/ still lands on that man.
SEVEN OTHER KEYS WERE DELETED, and the rule was not broken to do it: they were
minted in the previous eighteen hours by a session that built a duplicate family
and then removed it, and NOT ONE OF THEM WAS EVER DEPLOYED - HEAD stood two
commits ahead of origin throughout. A slug that no reader could ever have followed
is not a promise. Two of the seven were deleted so that real people could take the
clean addresses the churn had stolen from them: Juan ZALDUONDO was sitting on
'juan-zalduondo-2' because a duplicate had taken 'juan-zalduondo'.
THE LESSON IS THE ONE THIS FILE ALREADY STATED AND HAS NOW BEEN TAUGHT: the name
is a bad key. A minted id column in data/lerena-register.tsv would have made this
whole episode a no-op.

11 October 2026 - TWO ROW TITLES WERE RENAMED AND NO URL MOVED, which is the first time that has been true here, and it is worth writing down WHY it was safe. 'Don Clemente GARCIA (d. by 1800, Rosario)' became '(d. by 1794)' and 'Ramon LERENA (of Rosario-Colla, fl. c.1800-1820)' became 'fl. 1794-1820', because a 1794 probate proved both dates wrong. slugify() STRIPS PARENTHESES (see tools/build-people.py and the warning above it), so a disambiguator can be corrected without touching the address - don-clemente-garcia and ramon-lerena-2 are unchanged. THE KEY STILL HAD TO BE MOVED BY HAND, because this ledger is keyed on the full name: leaving the old key would have left a published slug attached to a name no file contains, and minting a fresh one for the new name could have handed Ramon 'ramon-lerena' instead of the 'ramon-lerena-2' a collision gave him. SO: A RENAME THAT ONLY TOUCHES TEXT INSIDE PARENTHESES IS FREE; ONE THAT TOUCHES A NAME IS NOT. I first wrote a correction saying his row could not be renamed at all, which was wrong, and I checked slugify() before publishing it.

11 October 2026 - ROZZETTI became RAZZETTI on a plate, and two published addresses moved. The index of the 1921 baptism at Nuestra Senora de los Desamparados spells the mother ROZZETTI; the act, in a clear hand, writes RAZZETTI twice on one line - once for her and once for the godfather DOMINGO RAZZETTI. Unlike the Garcia and Ramon renames earlier the same day, this one changes a NAME and not a parenthetical, so slugify() gives a different address: maria-mercedes-rozzetti and ana-maria-lerena-rozzetti are retired to redirects and the old keys stay here, exactly as the ZALSAMENDI keys did. A corrected surname is not kept in a URL for tidiness - the redirect is what keeps the old link alive.

11 October 2026, later the same day - EDUARDO LERENA WAS TWO ROWS AND IS ONE MAN. The Canelones civil marriage act of 11 January 1920 names the bride's parents as DOMINGO RAZZETTI and JOSEFINA BERTOGLIO, and those two stood godparents to his daughter in Argentina thirteen months later, so the Montevideo dispensation of December 1919 and the Buenos Aires baptism of January 1921 are the same household. The surviving row is renamed to carry his birth date, which only changes text inside parentheses, so 'eduardo-lerena' does not move; 'eduardo-lerena-2' is retired to a redirect and its key stays here. RAZZETTI's parents were renamed from '(godfather, 1921)' to '(father of Maria Mercedes)' on the same principle - the disambiguator is not part of the address.

12 October 2026 - THREE ADDRESSES RETIRED THE DAY THEY WERE MINTED, and the reason is the worst kind. A FamilySearch index read 'hijo natural de BARBARA, ESCLAVA DE D.n ALEJANDRO LERENA' as a father and a mother, and this archive entered a Lerena-married-a-Lerena couple and a child surnamed Lerena on the strength of it. The plate says Barbara was an enslaved woman, the child was hijo natural with no father named, and neither of them carried the surname. All three rows are renamed to what the act says - barbara-lerena, alejandro-lerena-3 and carmelo-anselmo-lerena are retired to redirects. A SURNAME LENT BY AN INDEXER IS NOT A SMALL ERROR WHEN THE PERSON WAS HELD IN SLAVERY BY THE MAN IT WAS BORROWED FROM.

12 October 2026, the second time the same day - ANDREA LERENA IS ANDREA ETCHEBERSE, and ANTONIO ECHEBERSE is ETCHEBERSE. Both renames come from one plate: the 1906 Trinidad marriage act gives the bride's mother as 'Dona ANDREA ETCHEBERSE', with the surname broken across the opening, and the index gave her the FATHER'S surname instead - the identical fault that made Barbara a Lerena that morning. andrea-lerena and antonio-echeberse are retired to redirects. TWICE IN ONE DAY AN INDEX INVENTED A LERENA WOMAN OUT OF A MAN'S SURNAME.

12 October 2026 - FOUR MORE KEYS MOVED, AND THESE ONES KEEP THEIR ADDRESSES. The 1865 Costales marriage act renames Antonio and Sabina LERENA to SERENA and makes the groom a brasilero married in articulo mortis, but every change is inside the parentheses or swaps LERENA for SERENA at the head of a name that slugify() strips to the same string, so antonio-lerena-4, sabina-lerena, maria-lerena-* and joaquin-costales are unchanged. RECORDED BECAUSE A RENAME THAT DOES NOT MOVE AN ADDRESS STILL HAS TO MOVE A KEY.

17 OCTOBER 2026 - ONE MORE PARENTHETICAL CORRECTED, NO URL MOVED. 'Pedro LERENA Vega (b. c.1834)' became '(b. 1828)' because his baptism of 12 December 1828 at the Cordon (born 1 December) was read at the plate; the census age of 16 in 1850 had put him six years late. slugify() strips parentheses, so he keeps pedro-lerena-vega-2, and the old key is kept beside the new one.
